text:
sam: deploy-bot flagged a blocked promotion to prod for release 2026.03.20-RC3 — canary failed during post-deploy checks, marking as blocking release

deploy-bot: Promotion attempt #3 -> FAILURE. Reason: artifact fetch error from registry. See ci-bot logs.

ci-bot: e2e-canary-3 timed out on step `smoke-login` and there are repeated 404s fetching layer blobs. Pipeline: https://ci.internal/redwood/pipelines/1423

alex: 404s look like registry cache TTL eviction + stale index. Happened after a GC window earlier today?

maria: I rechecked the registry logs — we see: ```ERROR fetch_blob: blob mount failed: blob not found sha256:4f3c9a...
client=requester-197, cache-ttl=0s```

jordan: ugh, CI is trying to pull the exact digest pinned in the manifest. If the blob was GC'd we'll need to re-upload or repush the image with a new digest.

devops-oncall: We can temporarily extend the GC grace window and re-run promote, but that needs infra change and a short maintenance window (5-10m). Ops prefers doing this in the 1pm-2pm UTC change window.

sam: We're on a release path that needs to go out before EOD. Options: (1) re-upload missing blobs for RC3 (hotfix) and re-run canary now, (2) rollback/pin to RC2 which is healthy, (3) wait for change window to extend GC and retry. Thoughts? @alex @maria

alex: Option 1 is fastest if maria can re-upload artifacts. It avoids a rollback and release notes churn. Two caveats: need to ensure manifests and tags are consistent; CI may have cached old manifests locally.

maria: I can re-upload the missing layer and a repushed manifest under the same tag. Command I'll run: ```s3cli put-object --bucket registrystorage --key blobs/4f3c9a... --file layer.tar.gz``` Then `registryctl refresh-manifest <repo>:2026.03.20-RC3`

ci-bot: Note — there are flaky e2e timeouts reported historically on `smoke-login` at ~5% on canary parallel runs. If we re-run only 1 canary, might still hit flake. Recommend running the full canary set (3 runs) or use a canary with increased timeout.

jordan: Good call. If we re-run 3 canaries sequentially it adds ~12m. That's acceptable. If maria can re-upload now, I'll queue the re-run and bump the e2e timeout to 6m for these runs.

devops-oncall: FYI extending GC grace or changing registry TTL would be safer longer-term but requires the change window and a quick postmortem. For this release I approve manual blob reupload and targeted re-run. :thumbsup:

sam: OK plan: maria re-uploads blob + refresh manifest (do it now), jordan will kick off 3 sequential canary runs with timeout bumped, alex will monitor registry and CI logs, I'll hold the promotion until 3 green canaries. If any fail, we fall back to RC2 and cut a rollback note. Agreed?

maria: starting re-upload now. I'll paste commands and upload ID when done.

maria: upload complete — object key blobs/4f3c9a... size=28.3MB. Ran `registryctl refresh-manifest` and got 200 OK.

jordan: queued canary-run 1/3 with bumped timeout. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/1423/console. Running...

ci-bot: canary-run-1 -> PASSED (smoke-login ok).

jordan: canary-run-2 -> PASSED. canary-run-3 -> RUNNING.

ci-bot: canary-run-3 -> FAILED (timeout on `payment-smoke`, retrying once). Error is a test flake unrelated to artifact fetch.

alex: payment-smoke flakes are known — we saw a change earlier to test fixture that increased noise. Not blocking unless repeated.

jordan: re-ran canary-run-3 -> PASSED now. All 3 canaries green.

sam: Great. I'm unblocking the promotion and proceeding with release. Notes for release: include item that we did a manual blob re-upload due to registry GC evicting a layer; infra will patch GC grace to avoid repeat. Action items: devops-oncall to schedule GC grace extension in change window and follow up with a postmortem. I'll add to release notes.

devops-oncall: I'll create the infra ticket and schedule the change. Tagging: @oncall, @platform-team.

sam: Thanks everyone — let's ship. :tada:
